measure: K is the RPN length: one token for each leaf and each eml.
branch: ln of a negative real, including both signs of a zero imaginary part, uses arg −π. Programs that pass through ln 0 stay singular.

domains.minus: exact for Im y in [-pi, pi) on this cut; the calculator uses rotSub elsewhere
domains.sub: exact for Im y in [-pi, pi) on this cut; the calculator uses rotSub elsewhere
domains.add: exact for Im(x+y) in (−π, π]; add(0, −iπ) = +iπ. The calculator uses rotSub elsewhere
domains.pow: principal value, the same branch as sqrt; (−1)^(1/2) = +i

records.0: K 7, proven minimal. All programs with K ≤ 5 are excluded. Lower cut, Arg in [−π, π), towers included, with or without ln 0 = −∞. On this cut −iπ becomes +iπ under the principal Log. See docs/minimality.md.
records.-1: K 15, proven minimal (uses ln 0). All programs with K ≤ 13 are excluded. Without ln 0, K 17 is proven minimal. Lower cut, Arg in [−π, π), ln 0 = −∞. On this cut −iπ becomes +iπ under the principal Log. See docs/minimality.md.
records.2: K 19, proven minimal. All 2056 programs with K ≤ 17 are decided. The word does not use ln 0. Lower cut, Arg in [−π, π), ln 0 = −∞. On this cut −iπ becomes +iπ under the principal Log. See docs/minimality.md.
records.ipi: K 21, shortest known. Lower cut, Arg in [−π, π), ln 0 = −∞. Under this cut (lower bank) this word is +iπ; under the principal log it is −iπ. On this cut −iπ becomes +iπ under the principal Log. Without ln 0 = −∞, +iπ on this cut (−iπ principal) is shortest known at K 23. Unresolved tower trees remain, so neither length is proven minimal. No −iπ on this cut (+iπ principal) is known with K ≤ 29, with or without ln 0 = −∞; unresolved trees remain from K 23, so no lower bound beyond K 21 is proven. The shortest known −iπ on this cut is K 45 with ln 0, and K 55 without ln 0.
records.-2: K 25, shortest known. Depends on ln 0 = −∞. Unresolved tower trees remain, so the length is not proven minimal. Without that value, K 27 is the shortest known (exhaustive search with unresolved cases).
records.-1/2: K 29, shortest known (exhaustive search with unresolved cases). Depends on ln 0 = −∞. Without that value, K 31 is the shortest known (not proven): 1111111EEE1EE11E1EEE11E1E1EEE1E. It does not need ln 0 = −∞, and it is exactly −1/2 under both conventions.
records.1/2: K 29, shortest known (exhaustive search with unresolved cases). Depends on ln 0 = −∞.
records.1/2-strict: K 31, shortest known (not proven). Does not need ln 0 = −∞. A second exact 1/2 word of the same length, also without ln 0, is 1111111E1E1EEE1EE11E1E1EE1EEE1E. −2, ±1/2, and 3 have the same value under both branch conventions. i (K 57), π (K 93), √2 (K 61), and ln 2 (K 25) are constructions, not search records.
records.-iπ-lower: K 45 on the lower cut, shortest known, not proven minimal. Depends on ln 0 = −∞. Not the K 21 word: that word is +iπ on this cut and −iπ under the principal log. The stored word is -ipi. Without ln 0, K 55 is shortest known, not proven minimal. The stored word is -ipi-strict. The word lies on the negative axis and comes out as +iπ under the principal Log at some precisions.
records.4: K 39, shortest known, not proven minimal. Does not use ln 0. The stored word is 4.
records.2/3: K 39, shortest known, not proven minimal. Does not use ln 0. The stored word is 2/3.
records.-1/3: K 41, shortest known, not proven minimal. Does not use ln 0. The stored word is -1/3. A shorter float hit is not this value.
records.-3: K 35, shortest known, not proven minimal. Does not use ln 0. The stored word is -3.
records.1/3: K 35, shortest known, not proven minimal. Depends on ln 0 = −∞. The stored word is 1/3. Without ln 0, K 37 is shortest known: 1/3-strict.
records.scaled-sub: K 565, shortest known construction of scaled variable subtraction. Depends on ln 0 = −∞. Not proven minimal.
records.scaled-add: K 655, shortest known construction of scaled variable addition. Depends on ln 0 = −∞. Not proven minimal.
